title: Remove unresolvable secinto/checkfix_utils module dependency
description:
go.mod requires `secinto/checkfix_utils v0.1.2` with `replace secinto/checkfix_utils => ../checkfix_utils`.
Two blocking problems:
1. The sibling directory `../checkfix_utils` does not exist in this checkout.
2. `secinto/checkfix_utils` is a malformed module path (no dot in first path element), so it can never be resolved from a proxy and `go mod tidy` always fails -> go.sum stays permanently stale (missing golang.org/x/net, golang/groupcache, antchfx/xpath, golang.org/x/sys entries).

Symptoms: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `go mod tidy` all fail on a clean clone.

Proposal: drop the dependency. Only two symbols are used:
- `utils.NewLogger()` (validate/validator.go:42) -> the Logger interface already exists in validate/types.go, reimplement locally (back it with logrus so CLI flags -v/-silent/-no-color actually apply, see csp-validator-fn-loggers-flags).
- `utils.ReadPlainTextFileByLines()` (validate/implementations.go:51) -> ~10 lines of line scanning; return the read error instead of silently returning an empty list.

Then remove the `require` + `replace` lines from go.mod and run `go mod tidy` (also prunes now-unused indirect deps: lumberjack, rotatefilehook, djherbis/times).
notes: Removed require+replace from go.mod. utils.NewLogger() replaced by validate/logger.go (logrus-standard-logger backed, so -v/-silent/-no-color now actually apply). utils.ReadPlainTextFileByLines() replaced by FileDomainSource.GetDomains() (trims whitespace/CRLF, skips empty lines, returns the read error instead of silently yielding an empty list). go mod tidy now succeeds: go.sum regenerated; pruned rotatefilehook, lumberjack.v2, antchfx/jsonquery+xmlquery, mattn/go-colorable. Verified in a scratch copy with the other 4 P0 compile fixes applied: go build OK, go vet OK, go test -race -cover OK, smoke test OK (INFO by default, DEBUG only with -v, missing domains file -> clear error + exit 1).
close_reason: Dependency removed, common functions reimplemented locally; tidy/build/vet/test verified in a scratch copy (repo build still blocked by the remaining 4 P0 compile beads).

title: Duplicate defaultSettingsLocation declaration breaks compilation
description:
validate/validator.go:19 and validate/options.go:15 both declare `defaultSettingsLocation`, with different values (os.Getenv("HOME") vs folderutil.HomeDirOrDefault(".")).

Package `validate` cannot compile: "defaultSettingsLocation redeclared in this block".
Left behind by Phase 3 commit 4cf94ce ("Remove Global State for Thread Safety").

Proposal: keep one declaration (the folderutil-based one in options.go), delete the other, and move the default to a csp-validator-specific config directory instead of the copy-pasted `analyzeResponses` path (csp-validator-sec-default-settings-path).
close_reason: Removed the duplicate declaration in validate/validator.go; only options.go keeps defaultSettingsLocation. Verified: go build, go vet, go test -race all pass (commit 8eaf57b).

title: Test package does not compile: unused variable g2 in glob_cache_test.go
description:
validate/glob_cache_test.go:97 declares `g2` and never uses it -> "declared and not used: g2" -> the whole test package fails to build, so no tests can run (and CI cannot be added before this is fixed).

Proposal: assert on it (e.g. `if g2 == nil { t.Error(...) }`) or assign to `_`.

Verified: with this plus the other 4 compile fixes, `go test -race ./...` passes and coverage is 44.9% of statements.
close_reason: glob_cache_test.go now asserts g2 is non-nil before checking cache.Size(). Verified: go test -race -cover passes (42.4% statements), go vet clean (commit 8eaf57b).

title: Undefined logger `log` in options.go prevents compilation (5 call sites)
description:
validate/options.go:81, 89, 93, 101 and 105 call `log.Fatalf`, `log.SetLevel`, `log.SetFormatter`, `log.Warnf`, but the file imports `github.com/sirupsen/logrus` (as `logrus`) and no `log` identifier exists.

Compilation fails with "undefined: log" (x5).

Proposal: resolve together with csp-validator-fn-loggers-flags (single logger that the flags actually configure) rather than only renaming the calls to `logrus.*`.
close_reason: All 5 log.* call sites in validate/options.go now use logrus.* (the package already imported). Because validate/logger.go backs the validator logger with the same logrus standard logger, -v/-silent/-no-color now take effect - this also covers the core of csp-validator-fn-loggers-flags (remaining part: gologger in cmd/). Verified: go build, go vet, go test -race, gofmt clean (commit 8eaf57b).

title: Unused fmt import in validate/html.go breaks compilation
description: validate/html.go:5 imports "fmt" but never uses it. Compilation fails with `"fmt" imported and not used`. Remove the import.
close_reason: Removed the unused fmt import from validate/html.go. Verified with go build/go vet (commit 8eaf57b).

title: govulncheck reports 26 reachable vulnerabilities (x/net, mholt/archiver, toolchain)
description:
Measured with `govulncheck ./...` on a tree with the compile fixes applied:

- golang.org/x/net@v0.34.0 - reachable through goquery's html parser (validate/html.go:34): GO-2026-5025/5026/5027/5028/5029/5030, GO-2026-4918 etc.; fixed in v0.53.0-v0.55.0 (needs goquery/antchfx upgrades too)
- github.com/mholt/archiver/v3@v3.5.1 - path traversal GO-2024-2698, GO-2025-3605, no fixed release; pulled in via projectdiscovery/gologger, of which only `gologger.Fatal` is used in cmd/csp-validator/csp-validator.go
- toolchain go1.26.1 stdlib - net/url, crypto/tls, crypto/x509, net/http, encoding/asn1, net/textproto; fixed in 1.26.2-1.26.6

Proposal: bump the toolchain to a patched release, `go get golang.org/x/net@latest`, replace gologger.Fatal with the project logger to shed archiver, and make govulncheck a CI gate (csp-validator-add-ci).

title: Silent fallback to a settings file belonging to another project (analyzeResponses)
description:
Two conflicting defaults exist (validate/validator.go:19 uses os.Getenv("HOME"), validate/options.go:15 uses folderutil) and both point at `~/.config/analyzeResponses/settings.yaml` - a copy-pasted path from a different tool.

loadConfigFrom() silently falls back to that default whenever the user-supplied --settings path cannot be read, so a typo in -s loads another project's configuration without any message. In the worst case it returns a valid ProjectsPath belonging to a different pipeline.

Proposal: single default `~/.config/csp-validator/settings.yaml`; if the user passed -s explicitly and it is unreadable, fail loudly instead of falling back. Deduplicate the constant (see csp-validator-fix-dup-settings-const).

title: domains_with_ports.txt entries are used unvalidated (scheme/host/port injection)
description:
validate/validator.go:191-199 blindly prefixes each non-empty line with `https://` and `http://`:
- lines containing spaces, control characters, userinfo (`user@host`), path components or extra scheme (`evil.com/x?@`) are passed straight to http.NewRequestWithContext
- no dedup, no syntax check, no host/port shape validation, duplicates cost a second fetch
- an empty/malformed file currently yields "No domains to validate" without distinguishing "empty" from "unreadable" (FileDomainSource swallows the read error - validate/implementations.go:51)

Proposal: parse each line with url.Parse + validate host[:port] shape, reject/skip-and-count invalid entries, de-duplicate (case-insensitive host), and propagate the file-read error from the DomainSource.

title: Untrusted page/CSP content is logged verbatim (log forging)
description:
Reporter output interpolates attacker-influenced strings straight into the logger:
- LoggerReporter.ReportSuccess/ReportFailure print the raw CSP policy (validate/implementations.go:49-56)
- ReportFailure also dumps the raw violation structures (SourceContext including inline script body bytes)
- logSummary prints raw host and error strings (validate/validator.go:446-478)

Values coming from a scanned host can carry ANSI escapes, CR/LF sequences and control characters, allowing log-line forgery or content hiding in aggregated logs.

Proposal: sanitize control characters (strip <0x20 except TAB, strip ESC/CSI sequences), cap the length of printed values, and prefer structured JSON fields over interpolated raw text (pairs with csp-validator-fn-json-output).

title: HTTP redirects ignore --max-redirects and have no scheme/host policy
description:
validate/validator.go:106-114 builds http.Client{Timeout, Transport} with **no CheckRedirect**, so:

1. `--max-redirects` (options.go:54) is only enforced for HTML meta-refresh (html.go:148-155, getCSPFromWebWithDepth), never for HTTP 3xx - Go's built-in default of 10 applies instead, so the flag does nothing for real redirects.
2. Redirect targets are followed unconditionally: any scheme, any host, including internal addresses reached through an attacker-controlled Location header or `<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0;url=...">` on a scanned page. In a pipeline context this is SSRF-shaped: a hostile page can steer the fetcher.

Proposal:
- implement CheckRedirect that (a) counts hops against options.MaxRedirects, (b) allows only http/https, (c) optionally rejects loopback/private targets behind a new `--deny-private` flag (default off so localhost testing keeps working)
- apply the same policy inside the meta-refresh recursion

title: Wire gosec G402: surface InsecureSkipVerify warning where it matters
description:
gosec reports G402 at validate/validator.go:109 for InsecureSkipVerify.

The flag defaults to false and a warning exists (validate/options.go:105), but that warning goes through the global logrus logger while the validator uses a different backend (csp-validator-fn-loggers-flags), so it can be invisible.

Proposal: emit the warning through the validator's logger when the client is built, keep the flag opt-in, add a reasoned `#nosec G402` annotation so CI gosec stays green, and refuse the flag for library callers unless an explicit override is set.

title: Project-name path validation only runs on the CLI path, not in NewValidator
description:
validateProjectName() (options.go:128-149) rejects '..', '/' and '\\' but is called only from ParseOptions().validateOptions(). Library callers constructing Options directly reach Validator.initialize() (validator.go:96-106) where BaseFolder = filepath.Join(ProjectsPath, Project) with no validation, then read <BaseFolder>/domains_with_ports.txt.

Proposal: validate the project name inside initialize() as well (defence in depth), keep the CLI check for early feedback. Additionally reject NUL/control characters, leading '-', and names > 255 bytes; '.' alone should also be refused.

title: Settings YAML parsed non-strictly; config validation failures only warn
description:
validate/validator.go:121-155:
- `yaml.Unmarshal` ignores unknown keys, so a typo (projects_path vs project_path) silently falls back to the default `/checkfix/projects`
- `config.Validate()` errors are only warned about ("Don't fail on validation errors for now") and execution continues, so misconfiguration surfaces later as a confusing "No domains to validate"

Proposal: use yaml.Decoder with KnownFields(true) and fail closed (add an explicit --allow-invalid-config escape hatch if backwards compatibility is needed). Return config validation errors from loadConfigFrom instead of warning.

title: Add CI pipeline: gofmt, vet, golangci-lint, go test -race, govulncheck
description:
No .github/ directory, no Makefile, no automated checks at all. Result: five compile errors were merged in 9555476 and nobody noticed, and the claims in IMPROVEMENTS_SUMMARY.md/CHANGELOG.md are unverifiable.

Proposal: GitHub Actions workflow on push/PR running:
- `gofmt -l .` (fail if non-empty; validate/validator_summary_test.go is currently unformatted)
- `go vet ./...`
- `golangci-lint run` (errcheck, govet, ineffassign, staticcheck, unused, gosec, bodyclose, noctx, prealloc)
- `go test -race -cover ./...`
- `govulncheck ./...`

Plus a Makefile exposing the same targets locally (csp-validator-add-makefile).

Blocked by the P0 build fixes: csp-validator-fix-dep-checkfix, csp-validator-fix-dup-settings-const, csp-validator-fix-undefined-log, csp-validator-fix-unused-fmt-import, csp-validator-fix-test-compile.
close_reason: CI pipeline (.github/workflows/ci.yml, Makefile, .golangci.yml) now exists and 'make ci' passes clean (gofmt, build, vet, golangci-lint, test -race -cover; govulncheck runs as an advisory job in CI). Required fixing two unrelated environment issues found while verifying: (1) a stray bare '/home/samareina/' PATH entry in ~/.profile collided with the ~/go workspace dir and made GNU Make's shell-less recipe fast-path fail with EACCES on 'go'; (2) golangci-lint was upgraded from v1.64.8 to v2.14.0 (local go was upgraded from go1.26.1 to go1.27.1, and old golangci-lint couldn't typecheck under the new toolchain) — .golangci.yml migrated to the v2 config schema and the CI pin (golangci-lint-action) bumped to v9.

title: Remove tracked logs/console.log (1.4MB of scan intel) and ignore logs/
description:
`logs/console.log` is git-tracked (1,458,893 bytes) and contains JSON log lines including historically scanned project names/host names from other tools. `.gitignore` does not cover logs/, so the file regrows.

Proposal:
- `git rm --cached logs/console.log`, add `logs/` and `*.log` to .gitignore
- consider a history rewrite (git filter-repo) to purge previously committed scan targets
- review committed `settings.yaml` (internal absolute paths, low sensitivity but repo-specific)

title: Process always exits 0, even when hosts fail validation or error out
description:
cmd/csp-validator/csp-validator.go only exits non-zero when Validate() itself returns an error (missing project / read failures). Runs where hosts produce FAIL/ERROR results still exit 0, so CI/CD pipelines cannot gate on the tool.

Proposal: add `--exit-code` semantics, e.g. 0 = clean, 1 = usage/config error, 2 = validation failures present, 3 = network/transport errors present (or a simple `--strict` flag making any failure/error exit 1). Document the code table in README and verify in integration tests.

title: Add machine-readable output: --json results and readable Report formatting
description:
Every result today is a log line, and failures print raw Go structs. Verified in an end-to-end run:

  [FAIL] Validation was not successful: [{... {1 false map[] [] false false true ...} ... [97 108 101 116 ...]}]

i.e. the inline script body shows up as a byte array and the SourceContext internals leak as unformatted Go syntax. There is no way to consume results programmatically (the plan document lists "JSON Output Format" as a pending Phase 5 item).

Proposal:
- validate/types.go: `Report.String()` -> "<blocked-url> violates <directive-name> (<element/context>)" and MarshalJSON emitting {document, blocked, directive, element, nonce/hash} without dumping internals
- new flag `--json <file>` writing ValidationSummary + per-host ValidationResult objects with a stable, documented schema
- keep the human log output unchanged for interactive use

title: Expose Options.MaxBodySize as a CLI flag (documented but missing)
description:
Options.MaxBodySize exists (validate/options.go:37, default 10MB) and is honoured by the fetcher (validate/html.go:166 io.LimitReader + truncation warning), but there is no flag - while IMPROVEMENTS_SUMMARY.md:376 documents `--max-body-size 20971520`.

Proposal: add `flagSet.Int64VarP(&options.MaxBodySize, "max-body-size", "b", 10*1024*1024, "maximum response body size in bytes")`, validate > 0 (and a sane upper bound), and surface truncation as a warning per host in the summary instead of only a log line.

title: Invalid numeric CLI values silently produce a no-op run or an infinite hang
description:
options.validateOptions() (validate/options.go:108-126) only checks verbose+silent and the project name. Verified consequences:

- `-c 0` (or negative): the worker loop never starts, jobs are pushed into a buffered channel nobody drains, allResults stays empty, the summary reports 0 hosts and the process exits 0 -> "validated nothing, reported success"
- `-timeout 0`: http.Client{Timeout: 0} means **no timeout at all** -> a single hung host blocks the run forever
- negative `-max-redirects`: depth comparison behaves unexpectedly in getCSPFromWebWithDepth

Proposal: require concurrency >= 1, timeout >= 1, redirects >= 0, body size > 0; fail fast with an explicit message instead of running in a degraded mode. Empty settings/project combos should fail similarly.

title: script/style-specific directives skipped; unknown directives abort the whole policy
description:
validate/csp.go:46-51 explicitly skips script-src-elem, script-src-attr, style-src-elem, style-src-attr and prefetch-src, so the browser fallback chain (specific directive -> *-src -> default-src) is not modelled. Two error modes:
- CSP3-specific allowances are ignored -> false violations (noise for the site owner)
- verdicts fall back to the wrong directive in the opposite direction -> false passes (missed violations)

Also validate/csp.go:90: any unknown directive returns an error, so the entire policy is rejected and the host is counted as an "error". Real-world directives outside the hard-coded list (e.g. fenced-frame-src, vendor extensions) kill the run for that host.

Proposal:
- implement the spec fallback chain per element type (script element -> script-src-elem -> script-src -> default-src, likewise for style)
- unknown directive -> log a warning, keep parsing, attach "unvalidated directive" to the report instead of returning Policy{}, err

title: Element coverage gaps: srcset, poster, srcdoc, form action, preload links, media sources
description:
validate/html.go only checks src/href/text of a fixed element set (htmlDirectiveElements, hrefTypes). Missing:

- `srcset` on img/script/source - multiple candidate URLs, none validated today (biggest silent gap)
- `poster` on <video> - falls back to media-src in browsers
- `srcdoc` on <iframe> - nested document, subject to frame-src plus all inline rules
- <form action> - form-action is parsed in csp.go but never checked
- <link rel=preload|modulepreload> - must map to the fetched resource's directive
- <audio>/<video>/<source src>, <object data=>

Keep the documented network-bound limitations (imported URLs, background-image in declarations, JS requests) as-is; the items above are all local decisions.

Proposal: srcset + form-action first (high signal, no network), then poster/source/data.

title: Security keywords silently ignored: strict-dynamic, unsafe-hashes, report-sample, wasm-unsafe-eval
description:
validate/source.go:118-135 accepts and *ignores* 'strict-dynamic', 'report-sample', 'wasm-eval', 'wasm-unsafe-eval', 'unsafe-hashed-attributes', 'unsafe-hashes', 'block', 'allow'.

Ignoring 'strict-dynamic' is the worst offender: with nonce + strict-dynamic the browser allows scripts loaded by an already-allowed script, while this tool reports them as violations -> heavy noise. 'unsafe-hashes' absence mis-scores hash-protected event handlers.

Proposal:
- implement 'strict-dynamic' propagation for script elements first
- implement 'unsafe-hashes' for inline handlers/attributes
- for the remaining keywords emit an explicit "keyword not evaluated - result may be inaccurate" warning attached to every report (and count such hosts separately in the summary)

title: Three logging backends: -v / -silent / -no-color do not affect validator output
description:
Log output is split across three systems:
1. github.com/projectdiscovery/gologger in cmd/csp-validator/csp-validator.go (fatal only)
2. the global logrus logger configured by options.configureOutput() (validate/options.go:87-106) - no validator code writes to it
3. the logger created in NewValidator (validate/validator.go:42, currently secinto/checkfix_utils)

Consequence: -v, -silent and -no-color only change backend #2, so behaviour is unchanged.
Verified end-to-end: DEBUG lines ("Following HTML meta redirect ...", "Final host: ...") appear without -v, and -v adds nothing to log levels.

Proposal: one logger behind the existing Logger interface (validate/types.go) backed by the logrus StandardLogger, so -v sets Trace/Debug level, -silent sets Panic level and -no-color formatter settings actually apply to every log line; drop the redundant backends. This also fixes csp-validator-fix-undefined-log naturally.
notes: Partial progress from the P0 compile fixes: validate/options.go now calls logrus.* on the standard logger, and validate/logger.go backs the Logger interface with that same standard logger, so -v/-silent/-no-color now DO affect validator output (verified: DEBUG only with -v). Remaining: gologger is still used for Fatal in cmd/csp-validator, and output format/colour behaviour deserves a dedicated pass.

title: Only the first CSP header is evaluated; report-only and meta CSP are ignored
description:
validate/html.go:187, 216 and 225 use `resp.Header.Get("content-security-policy")` -> only the first header value. Browsers enforce multiple CSP headers conjunctively (all must pass), so a second header that would block content is silently ignored -> false "success".

Never evaluated at all:
- `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` (deployed intentionally, should be assessed)
- policies from earlier hops of a redirect chain (only the final response's header is returned)
- `<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy">` (very common when headers cannot be set)

Proposal: return all values via Header.Values, parse meta CSP in the same HTML pass, and report a verdict per policy - page is failed if any enforce-mode policy fails; report-only results marked as such. Depends on parsing the document once (csp-validator-perf-single-html-parse).

title: Quoted source parsing breaks on '-' inside nonces/hashes (base64url)
description:
validate/source.go:157 does `parts := strings.Split(source[1:len(source)-1], "-")` and requires len(parts) == 2, so any quoted source containing more than one '-' is rejected.

Reproduced:
  ParsePolicy("default-src 'nonce-ab-cd-ef'")           -> error: unknown source "'nonce-ab-cd-ef'"
  ParsePolicy("default-src 'nonce-YWJj-ZGVm'")          -> error: unknown source "'nonce-YWJj-ZGVm'"

Because ParsePolicy returns an error, the whole host is counted as an *error* (not a violation), so sites using URL-safe base64 nonces produce no useful result at all.

Proposal:
- `strings.SplitN(inner, "-", 2)` and validate the algorithm is one of nonce/sha256/sha384/sha512
- unknown *sources* should degrade into a warning attached to the report instead of failing the policy (see csp-validator-fn-directive-fallbacks)
- add table tests with '-', '_' and '=' in nonces and hash values

title: Response bodies are read up to 10MB regardless of Content-Type
description:
validate/html.go:166 reads the body with io.LimitReader(resp.Body, maxBodySize) for every response, including JSON, images, downloads, archives and error pages that will never contain CSP-relevant markup.

Proposal:
- inspect Content-Type first; for non-HTML types only capture the CSP headers (cheap) and classify the host as "non-HTML, not validated" in the summary
- always drain/close the body (io.Copy(io.Discard, resp.Body)) to keep connection reuse
- for HTML, cap read size at MaxBodySize as today and record truncation explicitly in the result

title: Every host is fetched twice (https + http) with no dedupe, fallback logic or retry
description:
validate/validator.go:191-199 builds one URL per scheme for every domain, unconditionally:
- for hosts that answer on both schemes the same document is fetched, parsed and validated twice (double cost, near-identical results)
- when https fails with a TLS error the http attempt still happens - correct - but there is no retry on transient 5xx/timeout/ connection reset, so flaky networks produce ERROR rows instead of a clean failure
- no deduplication of the input list (duplicated lines in domains_with_ports.txt cost double)

Proposal:
- de-duplicate input (case-insensitive host+port)
- try HTTPS first; only fall back to HTTP if the TLS/dial attempt fails (still record which scheme worked)
- one bounded retry with backoff for 5xx/timeouts/EOF (max 2 attempts), classified as soft-errors in the summary

title: GlobCache keys can collide depending on the delimiter value
description:
validate/glob_cache.go:64-68 builds the cache key as `pattern` plus the delimiter rune appended as a string when delimiter != 0. That makes two different requests collide:
- CompileWithDelimiter("a/", 0)  -> key "a/"
- CompileWithDelimiter("a", '/')  -> key "a/"

A miss returns a glob compiled with the wrong delimiter semantics (in the cached-error variant it can also cache a permanent compile error under the wrong key).

Fix: key on a struct, e.g. `type cacheKey struct { pattern string; delim rune }` map[cacheKey]cacheEntry (or prefix the delimiter byte).
Add a regression test alongside the existing benchmarks in validate/glob_cache_test.go.

title: Hash checks recomputed per element; result slices unbounded and unpreallocated
description:
- validate/source.go:104 `HashSource.Check` hashes ctx.Body on every directive check; the same inline body is hashed again for each directive that contains hash sources. Memoise per-element (hash once per unique body content, cache in the SourceContext/validation run).
- validate/html.go `reports` slice grows unbounded: a page with thousands of elements produces thousands of Report objects retained in memory until the summary is built (no cap, no dedup - identical violations from the same directive repeat).
- several slices are appended without preallocation (golangci-lint `prealloc`).

Proposal: compute hashes once per element, de-duplicate identical reports (url + directive), optionally cap reports per host with a "+N more" counter, and preallocate slices from selection length.

title: Two full-document selector sweeps per page; merge into one pass
description:
validate/html.go runs `doc.Find` over the whole document 6 times (htmlDirectiveElements, lines 44-56) plus 5 more times (hrefTypes, lines 100-106) - 11 selector sweeps per page, each re-walking the tree with cascadia matching.

Proposal: build one combined selector per sweep ("script, img, audio, video, track, iframe, object, embed, applet, style") and dispatch on the tag/attribute inside the callback, or do a single walk with an element->directive lookup table. Doing this also gives stable visit order, which helps csp-validator-fn-report-ordering.

title: Each response body (up to 10MB) is parsed as HTML twice and copied twice
description:
Two full HTML parses per fetch:
1. validate/html.go:180 `htmlquery.Parse(strings.NewReader(string(body)))` for meta-refresh detection - the `string(body)` conversion copies up to MaxBodySize bytes
2. validate/html.go:34 `goquery.NewDocumentFromReader` in ValidatePage - second parse of the same bytes

and back in validate/validator.go:366 the body is converted to a string and re-wrapped in a reader again. With 10 workers x 10MB worst case this is meaningful CPU + allocation churn.

Proposal:
- parse once with goquery at the fetch/validate boundary and detect `<meta http-equiv=refresh>` from that same *html.Document
- pass []byte through without string round-trips
- short-circuit the meta scan with `bytes.Contains(body, []byte("http-equiv"))` before any parsing
- add a benchmark (go test -bench) so the gain is measurable - none exists today despite the claims in IMPROVEMENTS_SUMMARY.md

Related: csp-validator-perf-content-type-gating, csp-validator-fn-multi-csp-headers.

title: Custom http.Transport disables HTTP/2 and ignores proxy environment variables
description:
validate/validator.go:106-116 replaces http.DefaultTransport with an inline Transport that only sets TLSClientConfig + connection pool sizes. Two consequences:

1. When TLSClientConfig is set, HTTP/2 is only enabled if ForceAttemptHTTP2 is true - so every host falls back to HTTP/1.1 (no multiplexing, no header compression).
2. Proxy is nil, so HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/NO_PROXY are ignored - in proxied environments the tool either fails or (worse) goes direct instead of through the corporate egress the operator expects.

Also missing: ResponseHeaderTimeout, TLSHandshakeTimeout, ExpectContinueTimeout and MaxConnsPerHost.

Proposal: clone http.DefaultTransport (golang.org/x/net/http/httpproxy is already read by it), set ForceAttemptHTTP2: true, keep InsecureSkipVerify override, add ResponseHeaderTimeout (e.g. 15s) and MaxConnsPerHost ~= concurrency.

title: Remove dead code: unused validateHost, unused stylesheetValidator DI, Options.LastModified, ParseURL
description:
- validate/validator.go:275-322 `validateHost` is never called (golangci-lint `unused`) and duplicates validateHostWithResult line for line -> delete it (the result-returning variant is the live path)
- Validator.stylesheetValidator is accepted by NewValidatorWithDependencies and defaulted (validator.go:73-77, types.go:64) but never invoked - ValidatePage calls ValidateStylesheet directly (html.go:66). Either wire the DI point into ValidatePage or drop it from the constructor
- Options.LastModified (validate/options.go:22) is never read
- ParseURL (validate/validator.go:324-326) is a url.Parse wrapper used twice -> inline it

Each removal is independently testable with `golangci-lint run` + `go test -race ./...`.

title: No signal handling; results buffered in memory instead of streamed
description:
validate/validator.go:165 uses context.Background() with no signal handling: Ctrl-C kills the run without printing the summary the code already computes (the cancellation plumbing in CheckCSPForHosts therefore has no real trigger).

Also all results are accumulated in `allResults` and the channels are pre-sized to len(urls) (validator.go:177), so memory grows O(hosts x violations) on large projects.

Proposal:
- ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM); on cancel print the partial summary with canceled hosts marked
- stream each result to the reporter while aggregating counters only, keeping full Report lists solely for --json output (csp-validator-fn-json-output)

title: Violation report order is non-deterministic between runs
description:
validate/html.go iterates the maps `htmlDirectiveElements` (line 11) and `hrefTypes` (line 96), so report order changes run to run (Go map iteration is randomised), as does the concatenated summary output.

Consequences: diffs between two runs are noisy, golden-file tests are impossible, and severity ranking is meaningless.

Proposal: iterate fixed ordered key slices (or sort reports by element position, then directive, then blocked URL before emitting) so output is stable; add a golden test asserting stable ordering given the same input.

title: Add Makefile with build/test/lint/vuln/fmt targets
description:
No Makefile (listed as pending in CODEBASE_ANALYSIS_AND_IMPROVEMENT_PLAN.md section 6).

Proposal: `make build | test | race | lint | vuln | fmt | tidy`, with `-ldflags` injecting VERSION (validate/types.go:12) so `--version` reflects the build.

title: Reconcile CHANGELOG/IMPROVEMENTS_SUMMARY claims with the actual code
description:
IMPROVEMENTS_SUMMARY.md and CHANGELOG.md advertise work that does not exist in the code:
- migration guide documents `--max-body-size` (IMPROVEMENTS_SUMMARY.md:376) but no such flag exists (Options.MaxBodySize is hard-coded to 10MB in options.go:37 and never exposed - see csp-validator-fn-max-body-size-flag)
- performance metrics ("10x", "80-90% glob cache reduction") are unverified: no benchmark results committed, coverage measured at 44.9% with the concurrency/fetch paths at 0%
- "no more panics in production code / improved error handling throughout" while the package does not compile

Proposal: after the build is fixed and CI exists, re-measure, correct or drop the claims, and require a CHANGELOG entry per PR.

title: README documents a go-csp-engine API that does not exist in this module
description:
README.md describes module `github.com/secinto/go-csp-engine` and shows an example using `csp.ParsePolicy(policy)` / `csp.ValidatePage(policy, page, reader)` - neither exists here (module is `github.com/secinto/csp-validator`, entry points are validate.ParseOptions / validate.NewValidator). The example also has syntax errors (`url.Parse('http://example.com/bar/')` with single quotes) and the wrong import path.

Proposal: rewrite for the real interface:
- CLI usage and the flag list from validate/options.go
- a short library example matching actual signatures
- limitations list kept but extended with known gaps (nonce base64url bug, ignored srcset, skipped script-src-elem/-attr, only first CSP header)
